turns.doctor_question: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I've been having a hard time lately with... this scar on my wrist. I mean, logically, I know it's probably not as bad as it looks to me. But whenever I'm out doing things, like when I'm at church or sitting down for bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone's eyes go right to it. It just feels like it's the very first thing they notice about me now, and it's really been bothering me.

turns.doctor_question: When you are feeling this way about the scar, do you find yourself doing anything specific to try to check it, hide it, or seek reassurance about it?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I suppose I do. Before I leave the house, I’ll usually check my wrist in the hall mirror a few times just to see how it looks. I'll try pulling down my sleeves, or maybe I'll put on a bracelet to see if that covers it up better. And I do ask my husband sometimes if it looks obvious. He always says it’s barely there, but... I just feel the need to make sure.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors in response to appearance concerns, specifically checking her wrist in the mirror, attempting to camouflage the scar with sleeves or jewelry, and seeking reassurance from her husband.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself performing these checks or hiding behaviors because you are worried that something bad will happen if you don't, or is it specifically because you are unhappy with how the scar looks?
turns.patient_response: Oh, no, it's not because I think something bad is going to happen. I'm not worried about... well, a disaster or anything like that. It's really just because I'm unhappy with how it looks. I just feel self-conscious about the scar being visible, so I want to make sure it's covered up. That's really all it is.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms they perform hiding behaviors to make sure the scar is covered up due to their appearance concerns (excessive camouflaging).

turns.doctor_question: Has this concern about your scar caused you to avoid social situations or interfered with your daily activities?

turns.doctor_question: When your husband or others tell you that the scar is barely noticeable, do you feel like they are just trying to be nice, or do you genuinely believe they simply cannot see the defect as clearly as you do?

My husband is a kind man, so maybe part of it is him trying to make me feel better, but mostly I genuinely believe he just doesn't notice it. To me, it feels so obvious, like it's the first thing anyone would look at. But when he looks at it, or if anyone else happens to mention it, they act like it's nothing. turns.doctor_question: Have you ever sought out a dermatologist, plastic surgeon, or any other professional to discuss ways to have the scar removed or altered?
